filled_per_board.{{audience}}: the student's age, level and curriculum, e.g. '15-year-old IGCSE student' or 'US high-school AP Biology student'
filled_per_board.{{diagram_type}}: what is drawn, named specifically — only types the image model is allowed to draw (see image_types)
filled_per_board.{{view}}: the conventional view and its orientation, said outright
filled_per_board.{{parts}}: each part the student's level names: where it sits in the frame and what it looks like
filled_per_board.{{must_be_true}}: 3–6 positive, visible facts the picture must show (the same list the checker uses)
filled_per_board.{{labels}}: at most 6: the exact text (curriculum spelling), the part it names, its margin and row
filled_per_board.{{curriculum}}: one preset from curriculum_presets; 'international' when unknown

international.spelling: British English unless the student's locale says otherwise
international.names_and_units: IUPAC names (aluminium, caesium, sulfur); SI units

cambridge.spelling: British English (haemoglobin, oesophagus, fibre, centre, metre) but 'fetus'
cambridge.names_and_units: aluminium, caesium, sulfur; cm3, dm3, mol/dm3

us.spelling: American English (hemoglobin, esophagus, fiber, center, meter)
us.names_and_units: aluminum, cesium, sulfur; mL, L, M
us.conventions: Follow US high-school, NGSS and AP conventions.

prompt.purpose: A correctly labelled school-textbook biology diagram for one lesson board. For {{audience}}.
prompt.canvas: Landscape 3:2, plain white background. The drawing fills the central 60% of the frame; the left and right margins are kept empty for the labels.
biology_rules: Draw it the way a standard school textbook does: the conventional view named above, never mirrored.
Bodies and organs are shown as if the organism faces the viewer: its right side is on the viewer's left.
Draw only the parts listed, each once, with real proportions, positions and connections; neighbouring tissues in clearly different tones.
Membranes are continuous single lines; plant cell walls are double lines.
Oxygenated blood is red and deoxygenated blood is blue, only in diagrams of circulation; photosynthetic plant tissue is green.

rules: Write each label EXACTLY as given, once, with no extra characters.
Bold dark sans-serif, large and easy to read, set in the margins outside the drawing.
Each label is joined to its part by a thin straight ruled line with no arrowhead that ends on that part.
Label lines never cross each other or any label.

prompt.style: Flat 2D textbook illustration: clean, even dark outlines; flat colour fills; no gradients, shadows, photographic texture or 3D rendering.
prompt.text_and_exclusions: The only words anywhere in the image are the {{n}} labels. No title, caption, legend, numbers, arrows, watermark or other text.

prompt.purpose: A correctly labelled school-textbook chemistry diagram for one lesson board. For {{audience}}.
prompt.canvas: Landscape 3:2, plain white background. The drawing fills the central 65% of the frame; the left and right margins are kept empty for the labels.
chemistry_rules: Apparatus is a 2D side-on cross-section like an exam-paper diagram: uniform black outlines, glass walls as two thin parallel lines, no perspective, shading or reflections.
Draw only the apparatus listed, left to right in the order listed; every joint meets with no gap; tubes and wires connect to what they should.
A heated vessel or one collecting gas always has an open outlet — never a sealed system being heated.
Heat comes from a Bunsen burner flame under the vessel, only when heating is listed.
Liquids are a pale blue fill with a flat horizontal surface; electrodes dip into the electrolyte and are wired to the power supply.
Condenser cooling water goes in at the bottom and out at the top; a distillation thermometer bulb sits level with the side arm.
Any atoms shown use standard (CPK) colours: carbon black, hydrogen white, oxygen red, nitrogen blue, chlorine green, sulfur yellow.

rules: Write each label EXACTLY as given, once, with no extra characters; chemical formulas keep their subscripts and charges.
Plain dark sans-serif, large and easy to read, set in the margins outside the apparatus.
Each label is joined to its part by a thin straight line that ends on that part.
Label lines never cross each other or any label.

prompt.style: Clean exam-style line drawing in black on white, with pale tinted liquids; industrial cut-aways in flat 2D colour with clean dark outlines; no photographic texture or 3D rendering.
prompt.text_and_exclusions: The only words anywhere in the image are the {{n}} labels. No title, caption, legend, numbers, equations, arrows, watermark or other text.

image_types: device cross-section (motor, generator, transformer, relay, loudspeaker)
drawn_by_code_instead: Sankey diagrams and energy bar charts

prompt.purpose: A correctly labelled school-textbook physics diagram for one lesson board. For {{audience}}.
prompt.canvas: Landscape 3:2, plain white background. The drawing fills the central 60% of the frame; the left and right margins are kept empty for the labels.
physics_rules: Draw it the way a standard school textbook does: real proportions and connections; only the parts listed, clearly separated.
Devices are clean line drawings in cross-section or simple schematic view, never photographs.
Context scenes show objects and people from the outside, on a plain background, with no cut-aways.
No field lines, current arrows or force arrows: the teacher adds those afterwards.

rules: Write each label EXACTLY as given, once, with no extra characters.

Each label is joined to its part by a thin straight line that ends on that part.
Label lines never cross each other or any label.
